topic: Denmark is less English-taught than it looks
text: Denmark teaches many master's degrees in English. At bachelor's level it mostly does not. The University of Copenhagen — founded in 1479, with about 36,800 students — teaches all 78 of its bachelor programmes in Danish, and most Danish bachelor's degrees are the same. The English-taught bachelor's offering is real, and it is a specific and fairly narrow set of programmes rather than a choice you can make freely across the country. That is why this site lists the ones it does and not more: the list is short because the reality is.
attribution: The University of Copenhagen's own bachelor pages, read September 2026
whatThisIsNot: This is not a rule about you. If you have Danish at A level, or take Studieprøven, the Danish-taught programmes are open to you and the choice becomes much wider.
